title: Karnataka Launches AI University and Data Centre Policy | Govly
content: Karnataka Launches AI University and Data Centre Policy 🌐 Digital Infrastructure 🤖 Artificial Intelligence 🏛️ Physical Infrastructure 💻 Information Technology The Government of Karnataka is finalizing and set to launch a comprehensive Data Centre Policy alongside establishing India's first public sector-led Artificial Intelligence University and an AI Hub. These initiatives aim to strengthen the state's digital infrastructure, support AI research and talent development, and promote the growth and decentralization of Global Capability Centres (GCCs) beyond Bengaluru. The policy addresses critical infrastructure needs such as land, power, and sustainability for data centres, positioning Karnataka as a leading AI and technology hub in India. The Data Centre Policy will enable private sector investments by addressing infrastructure and operational challenges, creating procurement opportunities for data centre construction, power solutions, and digital infrastructure services. Establishment of the AI University and AI Hub signals increased demand for AI-related educational services, research partnerships, and technology development contracts. Procurement professionals should anticipate new tenders and contracts related to AI infrastructure, skilling programs, and innovation ecosystem support within Karnataka. Companies specializing in data centre technologies, AI software, and digital infrastructure should evaluate strategic engagement opportunities with Karnataka's government and GCCs expanding beyond Bengaluru. Global Capability Centres are no longer back-office operations. They are designing products, leading innovation and increasingly functioning as the second headquarters of global enterprises. — L K Atheeq, Chairman, Bengaluru Business Corridor Karnataka's vision is to build one of the world's leading centres for responsible Artificial Intelligence. — D.K. Shivakumar, Chief Minister of Karnataka Agencies Government of Karnataka, Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society, Karnataka State Government, Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Karnataka Digital Economy Mission The Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (Metro) Board has formally recommended governance reforms to the California Legislature aimed at enhancing regional representation and rider advocacy within its Board structure. Key proposals include adding voting rider representatives and permitting the County CEO to serve on the Board, aligning with anticipated changes from Measure G. An Ad Hoc Committee will further explore adding labor and small city representatives, with findings expected within 90-120 days. These governance adjustments could influence future procurement priorities and stakeholder engagement strategies for contractors and vendors working with Metro. Why this matters: Enhanced rider and regional representation may shift Metro’s procurement focus toward projects and services that better reflect diverse community needs. Procurement professionals should anticipate potential changes in decision-making processes and stakeholder involvement as governance reforms progress. Organizations engaged with Metro should prepare for increased opportunities to engage with new Board representatives, including rider advocates and local government officials. The ongoing study by the Ad Hoc Committee signals further governance evolution, which may impact contract requirements and procurement planning in the near term. ✅ Regulatory Compliance 💰 Grants & Funding 💻 Information Technology 💼 Professional Services 🚚 Transportation 🛡️ Defense & Military The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) has implemented new tariffs ranging from 10% to 12.5% on imports from approximately 60 countries that have failed to enforce U.S. prohibitions on goods produced with forced labor. Effective July 24, 2026, these tariffs target a broad range of products, with exemptions for certain raw materials and domestically available goods to avoid supply chain disruptions. This enforcement action follows extensive investigations under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 and reflects a strategic effort to uphold trade policy objectives and human rights standards. Several key trading partners, including the European Union, Brazil, Mexico, Australia, Switzerland, and Norway, have expressed concerns or opposition to the tariffs, which may influence future trade negotiations and procurement strategies. Procurement professionals should assess the impact of these tariffs on supply chains, especially for goods sourced from affected countries, as cost structures and availability may change. Government contractors and importers must ensure compliance with the new tariff requirements and consider potential adjustments in sourcing to mitigate increased costs or delays. The tariffs underscore the U.S. government's commitment to enforcing forced labor prohibitions, signaling increased scrutiny on supply chain labor practices that contractors should address in compliance and due diligence programs. Organizations involved in manufacturing, agriculture, and raw materials should evaluate exemptions and potential opportunities arising from shifts in trade flows and domestic sourcing incentives. ✅ Regulatory Compliance 🏛️ Physical Infrastructure ⚡ Energy & Utilities 💻 Information Technology Texas Governor Greg Abbott announced significant state actions to regulate data center development and protect residential ratepayers from infrastructure costs. Following the withdrawal of Diode's proposed data center near Cedar Creek Lake in Henderson County for failing to meet state standards, the Public Utility Commission of Texas (PUCT) and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) implemented new rules requiring data centers to cover their own electric infrastructure expenses. These measures include grid reliability enhancements and legislative recommendations to codify requirements for water efficiency, community impact mitigation, and financial responsibility. Why this matters: Procurement professionals and contractors should note the increasing regulatory scrutiny on data center projects in Texas, emphasizing cost allocation and environmental standards. Data center developers must plan for self-funded infrastructure contributions and compliance with water and community impact standards. Utilities and grid operators are enhancing oversight and reliability measures, potentially affecting contract requirements and project timelines. Legislative efforts to codify these standards indicate a long-term shift toward stricter procurement and operational conditions for data centers in Texas. Texas Governor Greg Abbott has extended the application period for the federal Workforce Pell Grant program, allowing more colleges and technical schools to offer short-term training programs aligned with high-demand industries such as construction, healthcare, IT, and advanced manufacturing. This extension supports expanded access to affordable workforce training aimed at enhancing job readiness and economic growth across Texas. The extension enables educational institutions to increase participation in Workforce Pell Grant-funded programs, creating procurement opportunities for training providers and educational service vendors. Agencies and contractors involved in workforce development and training should evaluate how this expansion affects demand for curriculum development, training delivery, and credentialing services. This initiative signals increased state and federal collaboration to fund short-term, industry-recognized credential programs, which may influence future procurement priorities in workforce education. Organizations serving Texas regions should consider aligning offerings with the Workforce Pell Grant program to capitalize on growing training needs in key sectors. 🚑 Emergency Response 🏛️ Physical Infrastructure 🚨 Public Safety 🏗️ Construction & Infrastructure Governor Greg Abbott conducted an on-site assessment of flood damage in Cotulla, Texas, and formally requested the addition of 30 counties to the Major Disaster Declaration to enable access to FEMA Individual Assistance programs. The Texas Division of Emergency Management (TDEM) is actively coordinating with federal agencies, including FEMA, to facilitate recovery efforts encompassing financial aid and emergency protective measures. The State Operations Center remains operational to support rapid response and recovery coordination across affected areas. Why this matters: The expansion of the Major Disaster Declaration will unlock federal funding and resources critical for disaster recovery, infrastructure repair, and emergency services procurement in Texas. Procurement professionals should anticipate increased contracting opportunities related to emergency protective measures, debris removal, infrastructure rebuilding, and individual assistance programs. Vendors specializing in disaster recovery, construction, emergency management, and related services may find new opportunities as state and federal agencies mobilize resources. Organizations involved in logistics, emergency communications, and temporary housing solutions should evaluate potential engagements with TDEM and FEMA as recovery efforts progress. Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers has approved an emergency rule permitting qualified Registered Nurses (RNs) holding a bachelor's degree and relevant clinical experience to teach clinical nursing courses. This regulatory change aims to address critical nursing faculty shortages that have constrained nursing education capacity amid ongoing healthcare workforce challenges. The rule supports broader workforce development efforts including training grants and expanded licensure for advanced practice nurses, facilitating increased nursing education throughput to meet state healthcare demands. This rule change enables educational institutions to expand clinical teaching capacity by leveraging experienced RNs, potentially accelerating nursing workforce development. Procurement professionals should anticipate increased demand for nursing education services and related workforce training contracts within Wisconsin. Healthcare contractors and training providers may find new opportunities to partner with state agencies and nursing schools to support expanded clinical instruction. Organizations involved in nursing workforce solutions should evaluate alignment with Wisconsin's evolving regulatory environment and funding initiatives to capitalize on emerging contracts and grants. Governor Tony Evers of Wisconsin has formally urged the state's Congressional delegation to support the reauthorization of the federal Farm Bill, emphasizing its critical role in sustaining Wisconsin's agricultural economy, including the hemp industry, and strengthening nutrition programs such as FoodShare. The letter highlights the need for continued and enhanced federal funding for dairy, forestry, conservation, and rural development programs, while calling for revisions to restrictive federal hemp laws that currently pose economic and employment risks to the state. Why this matters: Federal Farm Bill reauthorization will directly impact procurement opportunities related to agricultural support services, conservation projects, and nutrition program administration in Wisconsin. Procurement professionals should anticipate potential increases in federal funding allocations for state agricultural and nutrition programs, which may lead to new or expanded contract opportunities. Contractors in agriculture, forestry, conservation, and food assistance sectors should evaluate how changes in hemp regulations and Farm Bill provisions could affect service demand and compliance requirements. Organizations involved in rural development and natural resource management may find increased opportunities as the Farm Bill supports investments in these areas. 🌐 Digital Infrastructure 💻 Information Technology 🚨 Public Safety New Jersey's Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) has fully implemented automatic voter registration across all motor vehicle agencies statewide, complying with Governor Phil Murphy's legislation deadline. This system automatically registers eligible residents applying for driver-related credentials unless they opt out, electronically updating voter rolls with the Department of State. Senator Jim Holzapfel has raised concerns about the policy's impact on voter integrity, citing reports of non-citizens being registered and voting illegally between 2023 and 2024, and is advocating for suspension of automatic registration and legislative voter ID requirements. Procurement professionals should note the MVC's expanded role in voter registration technology and data integration with the Department of State, indicating potential needs for secure IT systems and voter data management solutions. The implementation reflects a growing trend in state-level digital voter registration modernization, which may influence future procurement opportunities for election technology vendors. Agencies and contractors involved in election infrastructure should consider the implications of policy debates on voter ID and registration processes, as legislative changes could affect system requirements and compliance. Organizations supporting state election systems may find opportunities to assist with system audits, security enhancements, and legislative compliance adaptations in New Jersey and similar jurisdictions. 💰 Grants & Funding 🏛️ Physical Infrastructure 📋 Contracting Vehicles 🛡️ Defense & Military ⚡ Energy & Utilities 💻 Information Technology Governor Abigail Spanberger led a week-long international economic trade mission from July 18 to July 24, 2026, to the United Kingdom, Italy, and France, focusing on expanding Virginia's trade relationships and attracting investment in key sectors. The mission targeted strategic industries including aerospace, defense, advanced manufacturing, biopharmaceuticals, agriculture, and energy. Meetings with over 30 companies and industry leaders emphasized Virginia's competitive advantages, workforce capabilities, and infrastructure to foster economic growth and job creation within the Commonwealth. The mission highlights Virginia's commitment to expanding export opportunities for agricultural and forestry products under the Farm and Forest Prosperity Plan. Procurement professionals should note increased international engagement that may lead to new contracts and partnerships in aerospace, defense, biopharmaceutical manufacturing, and advanced manufacturing sectors. Businesses in Virginia's supply chain and related industries can leverage strengthened trade ties to explore export growth and foreign direct investment opportunities. Agencies and contractors should consider the implications of enhanced global partnerships for procurement planning, especially in sectors prioritized during the mission such as defense and energy. Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger announced the commencement of production for the feature film "America's Favorite" in Coastal Virginia during summer 2026. This initiative leverages local Virginia crews and locations, supported by state film tax credits, to stimulate economic growth through job creation and vendor engagement within the state's film and television industry. The Virginia Film Office and Virginia Tourism Corporation are actively involved in promoting and facilitating this production, underscoring the state's strategic commitment to expanding its media production sector. Why this matters: Procurement professionals should note the increased demand for local vendors, production services, and workforce participation driven by state-supported film projects. The availability of state film tax credits incentivizes production companies to source goods and services locally, creating opportunities for Virginia-based contractors and suppliers. Engagement with the Virginia Film Office and related state agencies can provide procurement stakeholders with insights into upcoming projects and partnership opportunities. Companies specializing in film production support services, equipment rental, and location management may find new contracts and collaborations arising from this initiative.

title: Karnataka to set up AI University, to roll out tech expansion policy in 100 days
content: # Karnataka to set up AI University, to roll out tech expansion policy in 100 days ## Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar told industry leaders that his government will build an AI University and expand tech infrastructure beyond Bengaluru within 100 days. The push signals a broader strategy to spread investment, talent and digital growth across the state. advertisement Addressing CEOs at a breakfast meeting, Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said Bengaluru’s biggest strength lies in its talent pool and innovation ecosystem. India Today News Desk Bengaluru,UPDATED: Jul 24, 2026 17:47 IST Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Friday said the state government will expand world-class infrastructure beyond Bengaluru, set up an AI University with industry participation, and roll out new policies to strengthen the technology ecosystem. He also asked industry leaders to work with the government in shaping Karnataka’s next phase of growth. Addressing CEOs at a breakfast meeting, Shivakumar said Bengaluru’s biggest strength lies in its talent pool and innovation ecosystem, and credited the city’s rise as India’s technology capital to the people and companies based there. advertisement "You are the ambassadors of Bengaluru. You are the ambassadors of Karnataka," he told industry leaders, adding that many who came to the city decades ago stayed because of the opportunities and talent it offers. Among those present at the meeting were IT/BT and Home Minister Priyank Kharge, MLA and Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Limited Chairman Sharath Bache Gowda, Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan, and senior bureaucrats. Highlighting Karnataka’s economic performance, Shivakumar said software exports had crossed Rs 4.36 lakh crore and were expected to go beyond Rs 5.5 lakh crore this year. "Behind every number is a young engineer getting a first job, a developer solving problems, and a family moving closer to its dreams," he said in a release. He added that the state’s Global Capability Centres had moved beyond back-office work to become hubs of innovation, product development and high-value work. advertisement Recalling his interactions with global leaders at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Shivakumar said companies continued to prefer Bengaluru for its talent, ecosystem and cost advantages. "Many states are competing, but companies tell us that if it costs them USD 3.50 elsewhere, they can achieve the same here at nearly USD 1 because of Bengaluru’s talent, ecosystem and human capital," he said. He announced that within the next 100 days, the government would bring in a policy to encourage industries to set up operations outside Bengaluru by offering world-class office infrastructure at highly affordable costs, including office space in other Karnataka cities for as little as fifty cents per square foot. He said the government had already introduced new IT, Space Technology and Startup policies focused on DeepTech, digital infrastructure, research, industry-academia collaboration and entrepreneurship, and that Karnataka had also launched its Quantum Roadmap to speed up the commercialisation of emerging technologies. Shivakumar also said the state was building an AI University in partnership with industry. "Yesterday, we had detailed discussions with Google on this initiative. We don’t want the government alone to build it. We want to partner with industry. You should take the lead, and the government will stand beside you," he said. The university, he said, would be a centre for learning, innovation, collaboration and public digital access, with a vision to introduce AI education to rural students from Class 6 onwards. advertisement Shivakumar also announced the Bengaluru Robotics and Innovation Zone and the Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31, aimed at creating environmentally sustainable digital infrastructure supported by land, power, water, connectivity and renewable energy. Stressing balanced regional development, he said growth should not remain limited to Bengaluru. "Bengaluru is our crown, but Karnataka is our heart," he said, adding that Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi should emerge as major technology and investment destinations. The Chief Minister urged companies to adopt one government school each under their Corporate Social Responsibility programmes to improve infrastructure, classrooms, teacher training and learning outcomes. "We spend over Rs 1 lakh per child in government education. Yet we still have teacher vacancies. Government alone cannot do everything. We need your partnership," he said, adding that healthcare would be the next focus after education. He also acknowledged Bengaluru’s infrastructure and mobility challenges and said the government was addressing them seriously. Referring to the Bengaluru Tech Summit, scheduled from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre, he invited CEOs to take part actively, calling it "not just a conference, but a platform for policy, partnerships and outcomes". advertisement Shivakumar said the government remained open to suggestions from industry and reaffirmed its focus on lasting partnerships. "We are not looking for short-term investments; we are looking for long-term partnerships. We want to grow with you. If you are strong, Karnataka is strong," he said, summing up the state’s push to expand technology-led growth beyond Bengaluru while building new institutions and support systems with industry participation. - Ends Published By: India Today Web Desk Published On: Jul 24, 2026 17:47 IST Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar on Friday said the state government will expand world-class infrastructure beyond Bengaluru, set up an AI University with industry participation, and roll out new policies to strengthen the technology ecosystem. title: Karnataka to build AI university, hub, and data centre with Google support | AIM posted on the topic | LinkedIn
content: Karnataka Chief Minister DK SHIVAKUMAR has announced plans to build a government-backed AI university, an AI innovation hub, and a green data centre in the state. Speaking at Google I/O Connect 2026 in Bengaluru, he said Karnataka wants to become "one of the world's leading centres of responsible artificial intelligence." Shivakumar noted Karnataka contributes nearly 40% of India's software exports and hosts over 17,000 startups. He invited Google to deepen its partnership, saying, "I am ready to give you any support you want," adding that Google employs over 18,000 people in India, with 12,000 in Bengaluru. Google also rolled out AI initiatives for India, including on-premises Google Gemini access, Gemini 3.5 Flash, expanded language support, and new cybersecurity tools. title: Karnataka to roll out comprehensive data centre policy to support infra requirements of AI - The Economic Times
content: Bengaluru, The Karnataka government will out a comprehensive and sustainable Data Centre Policy to support the infrastructure requirements of artificial intelligence and next-generation computing, Bengaluru Business Corridor chairman L K Atheeq said here on Wednesday. Atheeq, who is also the financial advisor to Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar, made the announcement at the inaugural edition of the GCC Summit 2026, organised by Maxpo Exhibitions Pvt Ltd. in partnership with the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, and the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission, here. He said the policy would create the digital infrastructure required to support AI-led innovation and next-generation computing, while complementing the state's broader AI vision. "Today everyone is talking about Artificial Intelligence. Naturally, every organisation wants to embrace AI. But AI also brings significant infrastructure challenges. It requires data centres," Atheeq said. Stressing that data centres require reliable power and water, he said, "Karnataka is working on a comprehensive and sustainable Data Centre Policy, which will be rolled out very soon." He referred to CM Shivakumar's announcement at the Google I/O Connect event, where he said that Karnataka will establish India's first and largest public sector-led AI University, alongside a world-class AI Hub, on an approximately 100-acre campus. "Discussions are currently underway regarding the final location. The AI University we are envisioning will not resemble a conventional university with traditional departments and hierarchical structures. It must be a new-age institution-flat, multidisciplinary, inclusive and collaborative," he said. Alongside it, Atheeq said, the AI Hub will function as an incubation and innovation ecosystem, providing startups with a sandbox to build and scale AI solutions. According to him, the university will focus on four broad objectives: Building AI capabilities, conducting research into real-world AI applications, commercialising AI solutions to solve business and societal challenges, and creating public digital infrastructure for AI. "We want AI to address practical challenges in agriculture, education, healthcare, climate, governance and many other sectors," he said. He noted that the government itself is one of the largest repositories of data. "Yet we barely utilise this resource effectively. If government data can be responsibly leveraged, we can better understand citizen needs, improve service delivery, identify bottlenecks and significantly enhance governance outcomes through AI," he said. Pointing out that many startups cannot afford expensive GPU infrastructure, he said, "We must create shared access to GPU (Graphical Processing Unit) computing at affordable rates. We also envision a large public AI resource library that is open and accessible to everyone." He further announced that a Vision Group for the AI University will be constituted shortly with significant participation from the private sector, while reaffirming the government's commitment to expanding Global Capability Centre (GCC) growth beyond Bengaluru into emerging technology clusters across Karnataka. "Very shortly, we will constitute a Vision Group for the AI University. While the university will be public sector-led, it will involve extensive participation from the private sector," Atheeq said. He also highlighted that whenever Bengaluru is discussed, the focus inevitably turns to traffic and infrastructure. As one of the world's fastest-growing cities, Bengaluru is expected to continue expanding over the next two decades. To manage this growth, "we are pursuing two parallel strategies -- promoting growth beyond Bengaluru and making unprecedented investments within the city, with nearly Rs 1.5 lakh crore committed to infrastructure development." "I currently chair the Bengaluru Business Corridor Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), which is constructing a multi-lane corridor connecting BIEC on Tumakuru Road near Nelamangala to Electronic City via Yelahanka, Whitefield and Sarjapur. This project, valued at approximately Rs 25,000 crore, has already secured funding. Tenders for the first package have been completed and work has commenced," he said. "Once completed, over the next two to three years, this corridor will significantly improve connectivity between the airport, Whitefield, Sarjapur, Electronic City and other major economic zones," he said, assuring that major investments are being made in public transport. He said Karnataka alone has over 1,080 GCC units, accounting for nearly 30 per cent of India's total. More importantly, 34 per cent of India's GCC talent is based in Bengaluru. "Global Capability Centres are no longer back-office operations. They are designing products, leading innovation and increasingly functioning as the second headquarters of global enterprises," he said, adding that Karnataka remains committed to creating the talent, infrastructure and innovation ecosystem that will power the next generation of global enterprises. title: Karnataka considering setting up AI university, seeks industry suggestions: CM Shivakumar
content: * Higher Education * # Karnataka considering setting up AI university, seeks industry suggestions: CM Shivakumar The discussions also covered research, innovation and industry-academia collaboration; expansion of GCC investments beyond Bengaluru; strengthening Karnataka's startup and deep-tech ecosystem; and enabling GCCs to take on larger global mandates from Karnataka Bengaluru: Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Wednesday said the government was considering setting up an AI university and had sought suggestions from the industry in this regard. Asserting that his government remained committed to creating an environment where businesses can innovate with confidence, access world-class talent and scale globally, he said, "Together, we will ensure that the next generation of global technologies and enterprise capabilities continues to be imagined, engineered and scaled from Karnataka." Shivakumar attended 'Katalyst Connect: The Chief Minister's Meet with Global Capability Centre Leaders' here, organised by the Department of Electronics, Information Technology and Biotechnology, Government of Karnataka, in partnership with the Karnataka Digital Economy Mission. The event was part of the government's dedicated Ease of Doing Business initiative for GCCs, aimed at facilitating investments, addressing operational challenges and enabling faster coordination between GCCs and the government. "There is a proposal to set up an AI university, and we have sought suggestions from everyone. It is a new idea. Whatever the world needs, we want to provide it from Bengaluru, and the world too looks to Bengaluru for it. We have sought suggestions," Shivakumar told reporters after the event. Noting that more than 200 GCC leaders had participated in the event and offered several suggestions to the government, he said, "As you know, the whole world is looking at Bengaluru, and they have given suggestions regarding their needs here." "They have requested a mobility plan and have spoken about Beyond Bengaluru, centres of excellence, and the research and innovation taking place here," he added. Expressing happiness over the trust industry leaders had placed in Karnataka, he said, "We are prepared to match their expectations. They say there is a need to do more in terms of policy compared to other states. We will consider this, keeping their suggestions in mind." Keeping the industry leaders' suggestions in mind, the government would also work on how to develop Bengaluru and how to promote growth beyond Bengaluru, Shivakumar said. "I have told them that if they create more employment by setting up units in tier-II and tier-III cities, facilities will be provided to ensure they get land at a cheaper rental rate. We have told them that the government is committed to providing infrastructure if anyone wants to start operations in cities beyond Bengaluru, such as Mangaluru, Kalaburagi, Belagavi and Dharwad," he said. "We are not only thinking about Bengaluru; we are looking beyond Bengaluru. We will provide double the Floor Area Ratio for buildings in tier-II and tier-III cities to those who want to create jobs there, so that high-rises and top-class facilities come up there as well. We want to create a Team Karnataka with industry," he added. More than 35 per cent of the country's GCCs are present in Bengaluru, Shivakumar pointed out. Minister for Home, Information Technology, Biotechnology and E-Governance Priyank Kharge, among others, was present along with Shivakumar. According to a press release, the dialogue focused on strengthening government-industry collaboration and enabling GCCs in Karnataka to take on larger global mandates across artificial intelligence, engineering, research and development, product innovation and enterprise transformation. Addressing the gathering, Shivakumar reaffirmed the government's commitment to strengthening Karnataka's position as India's leading destination for Global Capability Centres. He said, "Karnataka's partnership with Global Capability Centres has helped build one of the world's most dynamic innovation ecosystems. Today, GCCs in our state are shaping global products, engineering breakthrough technologies and driving enterprise transformation." The interaction featured focused discussions on key themes, including AI, GenAI and enterprise transformation; talent development, skilling and future workforce readiness; digital and urban infrastructure; and ease of doing business and policy enablement. The discussions also covered research, innovation and industry-academia collaboration; expansion of GCC investments beyond Bengaluru; strengthening Karnataka's startup and deep-tech ecosystem; and enabling GCCs to take on larger global mandates from Karnataka, the release said. Noting that nearly 30,000 new vehicles are registered in Bengaluru every month, making traffic management a top priority, Shivakumar outlined several major infrastructure projects and said, "Overall, we are investing Rs 1.5 lakh crore in Bengaluru's development." Ahead of the strategic consultation, Shivakumar visited Target's India campus, the Global Capability Centre of US retailer Target Corporation. He interacted with the company's leadership and gained insights into the capabilities being built from Karnataka across technology, AI, finance, marketing, digital, supply chain, merchandising, store design and more, it added. title: Beyond Bengaluru policy in 100 days: K’taka CM Shivakumar - The Times of India
content: # Beyond Bengaluru policy in 100 days: K’taka CM Shivakumar Bengaluru: Karnataka is stepping up efforts to expand its technology ecosystem beyond Bengaluru. Chief minister D K Shivakumar on Friday unveiled a roadmap to develop emerging cities as innovation hubs while announcing an AI University and fresh policy support for deep-tech industries. Addressing CEOs at a breakfast meeting ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit, Shivakumar said the government would roll out a policy within the next 100 days to encourage companies to establish operations outside Bengaluru by offering world-class office infrastructure at affordable rates. “Bengaluru is our crown, but Karnataka is our heart,” Shivakumar said, adding that Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi should emerge as major technology and investment destinations. Shivakumar said Karnataka’s software exports have crossed Rs 4.3 lakh crore and are expected to exceed Rs 5.5 lakh crore this year. He added that the state’s global capability centres (GCCs) have evolved from back-office operations into hubs for innovation, product development and high-value engineering. At the Bengaluru Tech Summit curtain raiser, IT-BT minister Priyank Kharge unveiled Innoverse, a Section 8 company that will serve as Karnataka’s unified deep-tech platform, bringing together startups, academia, researchers, investors, industry and government. Built on a “triple helix” model, it aims to accelerate the commercialisation of research in aerospace and defence, electronics, space technology, biotechnology and applied AI. Karnataka’s flagship technology event, the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026, will be held from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) under the theme “AI & Beyond.The summit is expected to attract 1,800 exhibitors, 25,000 delegates, 1,000 startups and more than 60,000 business visitors from 75 countries, reinforcing its position as a leading platform for technology, innovation, investment and global collaboration. Kharge also announced an expanded Elevate Next programme, doubling grants for deep-tech startups to as much as Rs 1 crore. The first cohort comprises 33 startups selected from 983 applications, with grants worth Rs 33 crore, including 12 women-led ventures. Kharge said Karnataka was creating a regulatory sandbox to enable startups to build AI applications using government datasets, while also preparing a sustainable data centre policy and advancing its quantum computing roadmap. “DeepTech innovation requires more than funding—it requires a connected ecosystem. Innoverse has been envisioned as that platform, bringing together research, industry, capital, talent and government to help breakthrough technologies move from the lab to the market,” Kharge said, adding that the initiative would help startups develop, scale and compete globally. The government also unveiled MIST (Museum of Innovation, Science and Technology), a nearly 2 lakh sft museum dedicated to innovation and startups. The Rs 300-crore project will be developed under a public-private partnership model while preserving the site’s heritage structure. “Bengaluru is our crown, but Karnataka is our heart,” Shivakumar said, adding that Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi should emerge as major technology and investment destinations. title: Karnataka to roll out data centre policy to power AI ecosystem; plans public AI University
content: * Policy * # Karnataka to roll out data centre policy to power AI ecosystem; plans public AI University The policy forms part of Karnataka's broader AI roadmap, which also includes the establishment of India's first public sector-led AI University and a world-class AI Hub to drive research, innovation, commercialisation and startup-led AI development. Bengaluru: The Karnataka government is set to roll out a comprehensive Data Centre Policy aimed at creating the digital infrastructure required for artificial intelligence (AI) and next-generation computing, as it looks to strengthen the state's position as India's leading technology and Global Capability Centre (GCC) hub. Announcing the move, LK Atheeq, Financial Advisor to the Chief Minister and Chairman, Bengaluru Business Corridor, said the proposed policy will address the growing infrastructure requirements of AI by focusing on sustainable data centre development. "Today everyone is talking about AI. Naturally, every organisation wants to embrace AI. But AI also brings significant infrastructure challenges. AI requires data. Data requires data centres. Data centres require reliable power and water. Recognising this, Karnataka is working on a comprehensive and sustainable Data Centre Policy, which will be rolled out very soon," Atheeq said recently. The policy forms part of Karnataka's broader AI roadmap, which also includes the establishment of India's first public sector-led AI University and a world-class AI Hub to drive research, innovation, commercialisation and startup-led AI development. According to Atheeq, the proposed AI University will move away from the traditional university model and instead function as a multidisciplinary institution focused on four pillars - building AI capabilities, conducting applied research, commercialising AI solutions, and creating public digital infrastructure for AI. The accompanying AI Hub will serve as an innovation and incubation ecosystem, offering startups access to shared GPU infrastructure and AI computing resources that are otherwise expensive to build independently. "Many startups cannot afford expensive GPU infrastructure. Therefore, we must create shared access to GPU computing at affordable rates. We also envision a large public AI resource library that is open and accessible to everyone," Atheeq said. The government will shortly constitute a Vision Group with participation from industry and academia to shape the AI University's framework and governance model. ### GCC growth beyond Bengaluru Karnataka is also looking to expand its GCC footprint beyond Bengaluru by promoting emerging technology clusters in Mysuru, Mangaluru-Udupi-Manipal, Hubballi-Dharwad, Belagavi and Kalaburagi, leveraging lower operating costs, engineering talent and reduced employee attrition. The state currently hosts over 1,080 GCCs, accounting for nearly 30 per cent of India's GCCs, while Bengaluru is home to 34 per cent of the country's GCC workforce. Under its dedicated GCC Policy, Karnataka aims to attract 500 additional GCCs, create 350,000 new jobs and generate nearly $50 billion in economic output by 2029. Atheeq said GCCs have evolved from cost-arbitrage centres into innovation hubs undertaking product development, design and strategic decision-making. "GCCs are no longer back-office operations. They are designing products, leading innovation and increasingly functioning as the second headquarters of global enterprises," he said. Addressing concerns around Bengaluru's infrastructure, Atheeq said the state has committed nearly ₹1.5 lakh crore towards mobility and urban infrastructure projects over the coming years. These include the ₹25,000-crore Bengaluru Business Corridor, expansion of the city's Metro network to nearly 500 kilometres, development of 142 kilometres of suburban rail, and augmentation of the BMTC bus fleet to support the city's long-term growth. title: Karnataka announces India's first government-led AI University; AI education from Class VI
content: * Government Policies * # Karnataka announces India's first government-led AI University; AI education from Class VI Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar says the state will also establish an AI Hub, roll out a Karnataka AI Policy and set up two hyperscale green data centres to build an "AI-native Karnataka". Bengaluru: Karnataka on Tuesday unveiled an ambitious roadmap to position itself as an "AI-native" state, announcing plans to establish India's first government-led Artificial Intelligence (AI) University in Bengaluru, introduce AI education from Class VI, set up a dedicated AI Hub, formulate a Karnataka AI Policy and develop two hyperscale green data centres. The announcements were made by Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar while inaugurating Google I/O Connect India 2026 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC). In a post on X after the event, Shivakumar said, "Building an AI-native Karnataka. India's first government-led AI University in Bengaluru, a dedicated AI Hub, the Karnataka AI Policy, AI education from Class VI, and two Hyperscale Green Data Centres will power the next era of innovation." The proposed AI University will be developed on a 100-acre campus in Bengaluru, with regional campuses planned in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru. The university is expected to focus on AI education, research, innovation and industry collaboration to strengthen the state's talent pipeline in emerging technologies. To foster AI-led innovation, the state will establish a dedicated AI Hub as an incubation centre for startups, companies, researchers and academic institutions working on artificial intelligence. The government also plans to introduce a Karnataka AI Policy aimed at attracting investments and creating a globally competitive AI ecosystem. In a significant school education initiative, Shivakumar announced that AI education will be introduced from Class VI onwards. However, the government is yet to announce details regarding the curriculum, implementation timeline, teacher training framework or whether the initiative will be rolled out in phases. As part of its digital infrastructure strategy, Karnataka will also establish two next-generation hyperscale green data centres—one near Bengaluru and another along the state's coastline—to support the growing computing requirements of AI applications and digital services. Addressing the gathering, Shivakumar said artificial intelligence should be leveraged to improve public service delivery by helping teachers teach better, enabling doctors to diagnose diseases earlier, providing farmers with better advisory services, ensuring citizens receive government services with dignity and speed, and empowering small businesses to compete more effectively. Highlighting Karnataka's technology ecosystem, he said the state contributes nearly 40 per cent of India's software exports, while Bengaluru is home to more than 17,000 startups and thousands of Global Capability Centres (GCCs), positioning it to lead India's next phase of AI-driven growth. The announcements come as states increasingly compete to attract AI investments, research institutions and skilled talent while integrating artificial intelligence into education and governance. If implemented as proposed, Karnataka's initiative would create an AI ecosystem spanning school education, higher education, research, innovation, infrastructure and industry. title: Karnataka announces govt-driven AI university; pitches state as global hub for responsible AI
content: # Karnataka announces govt-driven AI university; pitches state as global hub for responsible AI ## The CM announced that the government will set up an AI hub as an incubation centre for research and development in AI by start-ups, companies and others ### By BL Bengaluru Bureau Updated - July 14, 2026 at 08:08 PM. Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar addressing the gathering after inaugurating ‘Google I/O Connect India 2026’ in Bengaluru | Photo Credit: Nalme Nachiyar Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announced that the state will establish India’s first government-driven AI University to become a global leader in responsible AI innovation. Alongside, the Government will also set up an AI Hub as an incubation centre for research and development in AI by start-ups, companies, and others. Advertisement Advertisement Making this announcement while inaugurating Google I/O Connect India 2026 in Bengaluru on Tuesday, Shivakumar said the proposed university would play a pivotal role in building world-class AI talent, advancing research and strengthening collaboration between academia, industry and government. “We want to build one of the world’s leading centers for responsible AI. Today, Karnataka contributes nearly 40% of India’s software exports. Bangalore is home to more than 17,000 startups, making it India’s startup capital. Our ambition is to make Karnataka an AI native state. So, we have decided to lay a foundation for AI. The first and the largest university by the government will nurture world-class talent,” Shivakumar said, addressing technology leaders, innovators, entrepreneurs, developers, researchers, and policymakers from across India and the world. As an AI-native state, AI is to be used responsibly to improve governance and everyday lives rather than remaining a technological slogan, he said. title: Karnataka Data Centre Policy Nears Completion
content: # Karnataka's Big AI Push: Data Centre Policy Nears Completion, AI University and Green Data Centres Gain Momentum Bengaluru has long been recognized as India's technology capital. Now, Karnataka is preparing to take an even bigger leap by positioning itself as a global hub for artificial intelligence. The state government is in the final stages of its comprehensive Data Centre Policy while simultaneously accelerating plans for India's first public AI University, an AI Hub, and Green Data Centre projects. Together, these initiatives could redefine Karnataka's digital economy over the next decade. In the AI era, software alone is no longer enough. Advanced artificial intelligence depends on massive computing power, secure data storage, and high-performance digital infrastructure. This is why governments around the world are investing heavily in data centres that can support next-generation AI workloads. Karnataka's latest move reflects this global shift and signals the state's ambition to remain at the forefront of technological innovation. The proposed policy is designed to create a strong ecosystem for artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and large-scale data processing. By offering a more investment-friendly environment, the government hopes to attract both domestic and international technology companies while strengthening infrastructure for homegrown enterprises. Once implemented, the policy is expected to accelerate the establishment of new data centres across the state. One of the most significant announcements is the proposed Public AI University. The institution aims to combine academic research, skill development, and industry collaboration under one platform. Rather than focusing solely on classroom education, it is expected to prepare students with practical AI expertise that aligns with the rapidly evolving demands of the technology industry. **Tech Vaidya WhatsApp Channel** Get AI updates, tech news, cybersecurity alerts and useful tech tips directly on our WhatsApp Channel. Join Channel **New Opportunities for Students, Startups and Investors** The proposed AI Hub is another major component of Karnataka's strategy. Access to high-performance computing infrastructure remains expensive for many startups and research organizations. A shared ecosystem could significantly reduce development costs, enabling innovators to build AI solutions without making enormous upfront investments. Such a platform could strengthen Karnataka's already vibrant startup ecosystem. The government's emphasis on Green Data Centres is equally significant. Conventional data centres consume enormous amounts of electricity and require efficient cooling systems. By encouraging renewable energy, energy-efficient technologies, and sustainable infrastructure, Karnataka aims to build digital capacity while minimizing its environmental impact. This approach aligns with the growing global focus on sustainable technology infrastructure. The impact of these projects is likely to extend well beyond Bengaluru. Large-scale data centre investments typically generate employment across multiple sectors, including construction, power, telecommunications, maintenance, security, and facility management. In addition to direct jobs, thousands of indirect employment opportunities could emerge through supporting industries and service providers. India is already one of the world's fastest-growing digital economies. As digital payments, e-governance platforms, cloud services, and AI-powered applications continue to expand, the need for secure domestic data infrastructure has become increasingly important. Additional data centres could play a vital role in supporting this rapidly growing digital ecosystem. Around the world, countries including the United States, members of the European Union, and several Asian economies are investing billions of dollars in AI infrastructure. Karnataka's upcoming policy represents an effort to position the state competitively within this global race. Bengaluru's established technology ecosystem, highly skilled workforce, and strong startup culture provide a significant advantage in attracting future investments. However, the success of the policy will ultimately depend on execution rather than announcements. Reliable power supply, land availability, high-speed connectivity, streamlined approvals, and efficient implementation will determine whether Karnataka can translate its vision into reality. These practical factors will influence investor confidence far more than policy statements alone. The final version of the Data Centre Policy is expected to provide greater clarity on incentives, implementation timelines, and infrastructure support. If executed effectively, it could strengthen Karnataka's position as India's leading AI destination while creating new opportunities for students, entrepreneurs, researchers, and global technology companies. As artificial intelligence becomes the defining technology of the coming decade, robust digital infrastructure may prove to be the state's greatest competitive advantage. title: Karnataka to Launch Innovation Museum, AI University, Boost Startups
content: # Karnataka to Launch Innovation Museum, AI University, Boost Startups By By Rediff Money Desk, Bengaluru Jul 24, 2026 16:56 Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge announces MIST, AI University, and increased funding for deep-tech startups. The state aims to lead in AI and innovation. Bengaluru, July 24 (PTI) Karnataka Minister Priyank Kharge on Friday announced a slew of initiatives, including the launch of MIST (Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology), the Innovers Foundation, enhanced funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, a proposed AI University, and the Nipuna Karnataka skilling programme, ahead of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS). The summit will be held from November 17 to 19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) under the theme 'AI & Beyond', the Minister who holds the Information Technology, Biotechnology and Home portfolios, said. The minister also announced the constitution of a Deep Tech Working Group, a Government First policy to make government datasets available to startups through a regulatory sandbox, and said Karnataka would continue to position itself as the country's leading destination for artificial intelligence and deep-tech innovation. "AI may be the current buzzword, but Karnataka has always led emerging technologies and will continue to lead the next phase of artificial intelligence. BTS will serve as a platform for policy discussions, strategic decisions and the preparation of a blueprint not only for Karnataka but also for the country," Kharge told reporters. Kharge said the government has launched the Innovers Foundation to mentor revenue-generating deep-tech startups, help them access global markets and facilitate the adoption of their innovations by the government through a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model. Reiterating that the next decade would be Karnataka's "Deep Tech Decade", he said the government has doubled funding for deep-tech startups under Elevate Next, increasing the maximum grant from Rs 50 lakh to Rs one crore. He said 983 applications were received, from which 33 deep-tech startups were selected and awarded grants totalling Rs 33 crore. Of these, 24 startups are from Bengaluru, one each from Hoskote, Udupi, Bidar and Hubballi, while five are from Delhi, Maharashtra and Telangana. "What is particularly encouraging is that 12 of the 33 startups are women-led," Kharge said, adding that grants ranged from Rs 85 lakh to Rs one crore. The minister also announced the formation of a Deep Tech Working Group/Vision Group, led by industry representatives, to strengthen Karnataka's deep-tech ecosystem. Announcing MIST, Kharge said part of the old NGF factory premises in Bengaluru would be transformed into India's first Museum of Innovation, Startup and Technology at an estimated cost of Rs 300 crore under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model. He said the project would preserve the heritage factory structure and would be designed by Dublin-based architectural firm Heneghan Peng, known for designing the Grand Egyptian Museum. Kharge said the proposed Government First policy would allow startups and companies to access government datasets and public digital infrastructure through a regulatory sandbox, with the government becoming the first customer for viable solutions developed using public data. He also announced plans to establish a state-of-the-art AI University, developed in partnership with industry, think tanks and private companies, to focus on skilling, upskilling, research and development, incubation and global collaborations. Drawing a parallel with the Indian Institute of Science, Kharge said the proposed AI University would create a globally competitive ecosystem for artificial intelligence, adding that a detailed blueprint would be ready within 15 to 20 days. Addressing concerns over AI-led job disruptions, the minister said the government was rolling out Nipuna Karnataka, which he described as India's largest reskilling and upskilling programme, with an outlay of over Rs 300 crore. He said the industry-led programme aims to ensure 70 per cent placement and 100 per cent employability, equipping professionals with skills needed in emerging technologies as automation and artificial intelligence reshape the workforce. Kharge also said Karnataka was finalising a framework for the responsible use of artificial intelligence in governance and was preparing a Sustainable Data Centre Policy to promote environmentally sustainable technologies such as liquid cooling while ensuring future data centres have access to renewable energy and adequate water resources. title: Karnataka unveils AI university, launches Innoverse as it expands DeepTech push ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 - Express Computer
content: # Karnataka unveils AI university, launches Innoverse as it expands DeepTech push ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 NewseGov Watch By **Express Computer** On **Jul 24, 2026** **0** **23** **Share** The Government of Karnataka has unveiled a series of initiatives to strengthen the state’s artificial intelligence (AI) and DeepTech ecosystem, including plans to establish an AI University, launch the Innoverse innovation platform, expand technology infrastructure beyond Bengaluru, and provide fresh funding support for DeepTech startups, as it announced the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026. The announcements were made during the Government’s annual CEO Breakfast Meet, which brought together more than 200 technology industry leaders, investors and policymakers. The event also featured the presentation of the Karnataka IT & DeepTech Landscape Progress Report 2025-26, outlining the state’s priorities across AI, semiconductors, biotechnology, electronics, startups and digital infrastructure. Addressing industry leaders, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said Karnataka was looking beyond attracting investments to building long-term partnerships with the technology industry. He announced that the state would establish an AI University in collaboration with industry to drive AI research, innovation and talent development, adding that discussions had already begun with technology companies on the initiative. “We are not looking for short-term investments; we are looking for long-term partnerships. We want to grow with you. If you are strong, Karnataka is strong,” Shivakumar said, while also announcing that the government would introduce a new policy within the next 100 days to encourage companies to expand operations beyond Bengaluru through affordable office infrastructure across other cities in Karnataka. The Chief Minister also announced the Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31 and the proposed Bengaluru Robotics and Innovation Zone, saying the government intends to accelerate technology-led growth across cities such as Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi rather than concentrating investments in Bengaluru alone. Alongside these policy announcements, the government launched Innoverse, a state-backed DeepTech ecosystem platform designed to connect startups, researchers, academia, investors, industry and policymakers through a unified innovation network. The platform will initially focus on Aerospace & Defence, Electronics System Design and Manufacturing (ESDM), SpaceTech, Biotechnology and Applied AI, while providing startups with mentorship, market access, strategic partnerships and funding opportunities. Highlighting the broader strategy behind the initiative, Priyank Kharge, Minister for Home, Information Technology & Biotechnology, and e-Governance, Government of Karnataka said the government was building an integrated innovation ecosystem rather than standalone startup programmes. “DeepTech innovation requires more than funding—it requires a connected ecosystem. Innoverse has been envisioned as that platform, bringing together research, industry, capital, talent and government to help breakthrough technologies move from the lab to the market,” Kharge said. He added that the state aims to create “a seamless innovation pipeline that supports founders at every stage of their journey.” The government also opened applications for the first cohort of the DeepTech Enabler Programme, targeting production-ready startups, and felicitated 33 winners of the ELEVATE NxT 2026 programme. Selected from 983 applications received from across India, the startups will receive grants of up to ₹1 crore each across sectors including AI, semiconductors, biotechnology, quantum technologies, advanced manufacturing, climate technology and space technology. BTS 2026, scheduled to be held from 17-19 November at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre (BIEC) under the theme “AI & Beyond”, is expected to bring together more than 25,000 delegates, 1,800 exhibitors, 1,000 startups and over 60,000 visitors from 75 countries. The summit will feature conferences and exhibitions spanning AI, DeepTech, semiconductors, biotechnology, fintech, spacetech and digital infrastructure, and will also host the inaugural embedded world India conference alongside the India edition of ChangeNOW. **0** **23** **Share** Express Computer Express Computer is one of India's most respected IT media brands and has been in publication for 24 years running. At a CEO meet ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, Shivakumar invited firms to partner in building tech hubs in Karnataka. Karnataka will introduce a policy within the next 100 days to encourage technology companies to expand beyond Bengaluru by offering world-class office infrastructure at affordable costs in other cities across the state, Chief Minister DK Shivakumar said on Friday, outlining the government's next phase of technology-led growth. Addressing more than 200 technology CEOs and industry leaders at the annual CEO Breakfast Meet ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026, Shivakumar invited companies to partner with the government in building new technology hubs across Karnataka. Advt "Within the next 100 days, we will introduce a policy to encourage industries to establish operations beyond Bengaluru by offering world-class office infrastructure at highly affordable costs," he said, adding that office space in emerging cities could be made available at prices starting from 50 cents per square foot. The CM said the government is looking to replicate Bengaluru's success in cities including Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi. "Bengaluru is our crown, but Karnataka is our heart," he said, calling for more balanced regional development. ### AI University Shivakumar also announced plans to establish an AI University in partnership with industry, saying discussions had already begun with Google. "We don't want the government alone to build it. We want to partner with industry. You should take the lead, and the government will stand beside you," he said. According to the CM, the proposed university will serve as a centre for AI learning, research, innovation and collaboration, with a long-term vision of introducing AI education to students in rural schools from Class 6 onwards. The government also unveiled plans for a Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31 and the Bengaluru Robotics and Innovation Zone, aimed at strengthening Karnataka's digital infrastructure and advanced technology ecosystem. Advt Shivakumar said Karnataka has already introduced new IT, Space Technology and Startup policies, alongside a Quantum Roadmap, to accelerate investments in DeepTech, digital infrastructure, research and industry-academia collaboration. Highlighting Karnataka's technology economy, he said software exports had crossed ₹4.36 lakh crore and are expected to exceed ₹5.5 lakh crore this year. "Behind every number is a young engineer getting a first job, a developer solving problems, and a family moving closer to its dreams," he said. Referring to Karnataka's Global Capability Centre ecosystem, Shivakumar said GCCs in the state have evolved from back-office operations into centres for innovation and product development, while Bengaluru continues to lead India's office market absorption. The CM also invited industry leaders to participate in the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, scheduled from November 17-19 at the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre, describing it as "not just a conference, but a platform for policy, partnerships and outcomes." Calling for deeper collaboration between government and industry, Shivakumar urged companies to adopt government schools under their CSR programmes to strengthen infrastructure and learning outcomes. "We are not looking for short-term investments; we are looking for long-term partnerships. We want to grow with you. If you are strong, Karnataka is strong," he said. * By ETGovernment Desk , * ETGovernment * Published On Jul 24, 2026 at 09:00 PM IST ## Comments What are your thoughts? title: Deep tech gets a shot in the arm, new IT policy and AI centre on the cards
content: # Deep tech gets a shot in the arm, new IT policy and AI centre on the cards ## The government also intends to set aside ₹300 crore for a Fund-of-Funds Updated - March 11, 2025 10:51 am IST - Bengaluru Shilpa Elizabeth Subscribe to The Hindu @ Just ₹1\* \*Offer only for new subscribers The government intends to develop start-up ecosystems in Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad and Kalaburagi. | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto The Karnataka government has announced that it will earmark a corpus fund of ₹100 crore for deep tech development in the State. Advertisement Advertisement It also intends to set aside ₹300 crore for a Fund-of-Funds, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah announced in the Budget on Friday. The announcement comes against the backdrop of demands for sector-specific and region-specific Fund-of-Funds ever since the launch of the scheme by the Union government in 2016 with a corpus of ₹10,000 crore. Both initiatives will be introduced under the Local Economy Accelerator Programme, which the government plans to launch to stimulate innovation and entrepreneurship in cities other than Bengaluru in the current year with a grant of ₹1,000 crore. LEAP will aim at creating 5 lakh employment opportunities. #### Beyond Bengaluru Under the programme, the government also intends to develop start-up ecosystems in Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad and Kalaburagi and set up incubators, accelerators, centres of excellence and Global Technology Centres. Sign up for free and get curated news updates LOG IN Support our reporting. SUBSCRIBE NOW In recent years, the government has been increasingly pushing to develop start-up clusters and build investor interest in cities other than Bengaluru through its ‘Beyond Bengaluru’ initiatives. In 2024, Minister for Information Technology Priyank Kharge revealed the government’s intention to create 10,000 new start-ups in smaller towns and cities in five years under the initiative. #### AI centre During the Budget, the CM also announced that a new IT policy would be implemented in 2025 with the aim of further strengthening the State’s presence in the It sector. “This new policy will not only give emphasis on cloud computing and development of emerging technologies but also expand information technology to tier-2 and tier-3 cities while reinforcing Karnataka’s position as a global technology hub,” he said. To make further strides in the field of Artificial Intelligence, the government is also planning to set up a Centre for Applied AI for Tech Solutions with an investment of Rs 50 crores over the next five years. The other major announcements include Global Innovation Districts in Mysuru, Belagavi, Dharwad and Bengaluru, three new GTCs in Mangaluru, Hubli and Belagavi, and an Agri-Tech accelerator in Kalaburagi. title: Beyond Bengaluru policy to be released in 100 days to attract investors
content: ### Beyond Bengaluru policy to be released in 100 days to attract investors CM calls for investment in AI, education, and plans to slash office rent Salar News * *Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw and Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan were among those present at the meeting (ANI)* Bengaluru, 24 July Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced that his government would unveil within the next 100 days a policy to expand world-class infrastructure “Beyond Bengaluru”, establish an AI University with industry participation, and launch new policies to strengthen the technology ecosystem. Addressing CEOs at a breakfast meeting, Shivakumar said the government will encourage industries to establish operations beyond Bengaluru by offering world-class office infrastructure at highly affordable costs, including office space in other cities of Karnataka for as little as fifty cents per square foot. IT/BT and Home Minister for Priyank Kharge, MLA and Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Limited (KEONICS) Chairman Sharath Bache Gowda, Biocon founder Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan, and senior bureaucrats were among those present at the breakfast meeting. “Many states are competing, but companies tell us that if it costs them USD 3.50 elsewhere, they can achieve the same here at nearly USD 1 because of Bengaluru’s talent, ecosystem and human capital,” he added. Discussing Karnataka's economic performance, Shivakumar said software exports had crossed Rs 4.36 lakh crore and are expected to exceed Rs 5.5 lakh crore this year. “Bengaluru is our crown, but Karnataka is our heart,” he said, adding that cities such as Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Belagavi should emerge as major technology and investment destinations, he added. **AI VARSITY** Shivakumar also said that Karnataka is building an AI University in partnership with industry. “Yesterday, we had detailed discussions with Google on this initiative. We don’t want the government alone to build it. We want to partner with industry. You should take the lead, and the government will stand beside you,” he said. The university, he said, will serve as a centre for learning, innovation, collaboration and public digital access, with the vision of introducing AI education to rural students from Class 6 onwards. He later told reporter that “we want to take AI to rural children” and the government was planning a curriculum for it. At the meeting, he urged companies to adopt one government school each under their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programmes. “We spend over Rs 1 lakh per child in government education. Yet we still have teacher vacancies. Government alone cannot do everything. We need your partnership,” he said, adding that this would be followed by a greater focus on healthcare. **DATA CENTRE POLICY** Shivakumar announced the Bengaluru Robotics and Innovation Zone and the Sustainable Data Centre Policy 2026-31, aimed at creating environmentally sustainable digital infrastructure supported by land, power, water, connectivity and renewable energy. The announcement comes in the backdrop of Bidadi farmers protesting against the Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township project, for which the government plans mass land acquisition to develop India’s first “AI-powered township”. ###### Share Now #### Leave a Reply Your email address will not be published. title: Karnataka Plans AI University, Tech Expansion Beyond Bengaluru
content: # Karnataka Plans AI University, Tech Expansion Beyond Bengaluru TECHNOLOGY AuthorAnanya Iyer|Published at:24th July 2026, 8:31 pm Add as a PreferredSource on Google Karnataka government aims to launch an AI University and a new tech expansion policy within 100 days to decentralize IT growth. The initiative offers low-cost office infrastructure in cities like Mysuru and Hubballi to attract investments outside Bengaluru. ## Detailed Coverage The Karnataka government has announced a strategic shift to expand the state's technology footprint beyond its primary hub, Bengaluru. Chief Minister DK Shivakumar revealed plans to establish an Artificial Intelligence University and implement a comprehensive tech expansion policy within the next 100 days. This move seeks to address the heavy concentration of IT infrastructure in the capital by incentivizing companies to set up operations in secondary cities including Mysuru, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru, and Belagavi. ### Infrastructure Incentives and Regional Growth A core component of this strategy is the provision of affordable office space in emerging tech destinations. The government plans to offer infrastructure at costs as low as $0.50 per square foot, a move designed to lower capital spending requirements for companies looking to expand. By decentralizing operations, the state aims to balance regional economic development while tapping into new talent pools across different districts. This policy is part of a broader effort that includes new frameworks for space technology, startups, and deep-tech sectors to maintain Karnataka's competitive position in the Indian IT landscape. ### AI Education and Industry Partnership The proposed AI University is intended to be a public-private partnership, with early discussions reportedly involving major technology firms like Google. Beyond higher education, the initiative includes a plan to introduce AI curricula to students in government-run rural schools starting from Class 6. By focusing on early education and industry-academia synergy, the state government intends to create a long-term pipeline of skilled professionals. The project also incorporates a Sustainable Data Centre Policy for 2026-31, emphasizing the need for energy-efficient digital infrastructure as the state scales its technology capacity. ### Investor and Sector Considerations For investors and companies, the success of this expansion will depend on the actual availability of power, high-speed connectivity, and skilled talent in these secondary cities. While the lower cost of real estate is a clear benefit, companies will likely assess the operational risks associated with shifting or scaling activities outside the well-established ecosystem of Bengaluru. Historically, infrastructure development in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities in India has faced execution challenges related to logistics and specialized talent retention. The government has scheduled the Bengaluru Tech Summit from November 17-19, 2026, which will likely serve as the primary platform for providing further details on these policy rollouts and potential partnership agreements. Investors may monitor the upcoming policy notifications for specific timelines on land allocation and the extent of private sector participation in the new university model. **Disclaimer:** This article is published for informational purposes only. content: ## Northeast Today's Post --- ### **Northeast Today** July 14 at 10:20 AM #NETSnippet | Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Tuesday announced plans to establish India's first government-driven Artificial Intelligence (AI) University and a dedicated AI hub as part of the state's strategy to become a global leader in AI research, innovation and talent development. Speaking at the inauguration of Google I/O Connect India 2026 in Bengaluru, Shivakumar said the AI University will be developed on a 100-acre campus in Bengaluru, with regional campuses in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru. The university will focus on nurturing world-class AI talent, advancing research and fostering collaboration between academia, industry and government. The proposed AI hub will serve as an incubation centre for startups, companies and academic institutions, strengthening Karnataka's growing AI ecosystem. The Chief Minister also announced that the state will soon unveil a dedicated Karnataka AI Policy aimed at attracting investments, supporting AI startups and building a globally competitive AI ecosystem. As part of the initiative, AI education will be introduced from Class VI onwards to equip students with foundational skills in artificial intelligence. To support the state's digital infrastructure, Karnataka also plans to establish two next-generation green data centres near Bengaluru and along the state's coastline. Describing artificial intelligence as the defining technological transformation of the current era, Shivakumar said Karnataka aims to become an "AI-native state" by integrating AI into governance and public service delivery. "AI must help teachers teach better, doctors diagnose diseases earlier, farmers receive better advisory services, citizens access government services with dignity and speed, and small businesses compete confidently," he said. Highlighting Karnataka's position as India's technology hub, Shivakumar noted that the state contributes nearly 40 per cent of the country's software exports and that Bengaluru is home to more than 17,000 startups. He also invited Google to deepen its collaboration with Karnataka in sectors such as education, healthcare, agriculture, climate resilience, urban mobility and digital governance.
