content: * GovTech Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar (Photo/File) Facebook X WhatsApp Linkedin **BENGALURU:** Karnataka has announced plans to establish what it described as India’s first government-led artificial intelligence (AI) university, as the state unveiled a broader strategy aimed at strengthening AI education, research, digital infrastructure and industry collaboration. Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar made the announcement while inaugurating Google I/O Connect India 2026 in Bengaluru, saying the proposed university would help build AI talent, advance research and strengthen collaboration between academia, industry and government. The government also announced plans to establish a dedicated AI Hub as an incubation centre for startups, companies and researchers, introduce a Karnataka AI Policy, incorporate AI education into the school curriculum from Class VI, and develop two hyperscale green data centres to support AI infrastructure. The announcements are part of Karnataka’s efforts to position itself as an “AI-native” state by expanding artificial intelligence adoption across education, healthcare, agriculture, governance and industry. “Karnataka’s vision is to build one of the world’s leading centres for responsible Artificial Intelligence,” Shivakumar said, adding that the state wanted AI to improve governance and public services while creating new economic opportunities. According to the government, the proposed AI University will focus on developing specialised AI talent, promoting advanced research and supporting collaboration between educational institutions, industry and the public sector. The AI Hub will function as an incubation centre to support research, product development and innovation by startups, technology companies and academic institutions. ## **Karnataka’s existing technology ecosystem** While the government outlined the broad vision, it did not disclose details such as the project’s investment, implementation timeline or governance structure. Further information on the university and the proposed AI policy is expected to be announced later. The proposed university is expected to complement Karnataka’s existing technology ecosystem. The state contributes nearly 40% of India’s software exports, while Bengaluru is home to more than 17,000 startups and one of the country’s largest concentrations of Global Capability Centres (GCCs). The announcement also builds on Karnataka’s recent efforts to strengthen its AI ecosystem. Earlier this year, the state approved an AI Centre of Excellence to promote deep-tech innovation and AI adoption across sectors, while its Startup Policy 2025-30 identified AI among the priority technologies for startup development. State governments are increasingly competing to attract AI investment through a combination of policy support, digital infrastructure, startup incentives and talent development as demand for AI skills accelerates across sectors. Karnataka, which already hosts major engineering centres of global technology companies, is seeking to leverage that ecosystem to strengthen its position as a hub for AI research, product development and commercial deployment.

content: # Karnataka Plans Government-Backed AI University, Innovation Hub And Green Data Centres Brief July 15, 2026 0 198 Facebook Twitter Pinterest WhatsApp Linkedin Karnataka has announced plans to establish a government-backed artificial intelligence university, an AI Innovation Hub, school-level AI learning pathways and next-generation green data centres as part of a broader push to position the state as an AI-native ecosystem. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar said the proposed AI university would be built as a major public institution for AI research and talent development. A public statement from the Chief Minister’s office described the plan as a 100-acre world-class AI university campus in Bengaluru, with regional campuses proposed in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru and Mysuru. The state also plans to establish an AI Innovation Hub to support research, startups and collaboration between government, industry and academia. Shivakumar said AI should be used carefully, responsibly and effectively in areas such as education, healthcare, agriculture, public services and small-business competitiveness. Karnataka is also evaluating two next-generation green data centres for AI infrastructure, one near Bengaluru and another in a coastal district. One location under consideration is Hoskote near Bengaluru, where a proposed 500 MW data-centre project would use secondary-treated water from the Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board and solar power from the Pavagada Solar Park. Mangaluru has also been identified as a possible coastal location. The state’s data-centre plans come amid rising scrutiny of the power, water and heat-management demands of AI infrastructure. Karnataka’s technology department has already been examining a sustainable data-centre policy, including site selection, renewable energy access, power evacuation lines and water availability. A committee of senior IAS officers has been formed to evaluate data-centre locations and infrastructure conditions. Shivakumar has positioned Bengaluru and Karnataka as a base for AI deployment at scale, citing the state’s software exports, startup density and global capability centre presence. The announcement also came alongside Google’s India-focused AI initiatives at I/O Connect India 2026, including developer training, sovereign AI infrastructure and school-level tooling. title: Karnataka wants to build India's first AI University. The bigger question is whether we need another university or more AI talent. : r/TechnologyNewsIndia
content: # Karnataka wants to build India's first AI University. The bigger question is whether we need another university or more AI talent. Bengaluru already calls itself India's tech capital. Now Karnataka wants to make it India's AI capital too. At Google I/O Connect India 2026, CM D.K. Shivakumar announced plans for: * 🎓 India's first **government-backed AI University** * 🚀 A dedicated **AI Hub** to support startups, researchers and enterprises * ☁️ More investment in AI infrastructure, data centres and hyperscale computing * 🤝 Closer partnerships with companies like Google for AI in education, healthcare, agriculture and governance On paper, it sounds like the next logical step. But here's what caught my attention. The announcement isn't just about creating another university. It's about trying to solve a problem India keeps running into. Companies are hiring for AI faster than colleges are producing people who can actually build production-grade AI systems. We've seen multiple reports this year showing: * AI job openings continue to outpace talent. * Companies increasingly want engineers who can deploy AI, not just use ChatGPT. * AI skills are expanding beyond software into finance, HR, healthcare and manufacturing. So the success of this AI University won't depend on how impressive the campus looks. It'll depend on whether graduates leave with real-world skills in: * AI engineering * Agentic AI * Robotics * AI infrastructure * Model deployment * AI safety and governance Because another theory-heavy engineering degree isn't what the industry is asking for. India already has enough degrees. The shortage is in people who can ship AI products. **Do you think India needs dedicated AI universities, or should existing engineering colleges simply overhaul their curriculum instead?** --- NissanUSA • Promoted Inside the Nissan Rogue journey: 24 hours of focus for a lifetime on the road. For example, if you search for **compute?**, the search engine will provide results that contain words such as computer or compute**d** but not compute**rs** because the question mark represents only one character. **NOTE**: Wildcards cannot be used at the start of a search term or when searching for phrases within quotes. #### Special Characters The following characters have a special meaning when they appear in a query: + - && || ! ( ) { } [ ] ^ " ~ \* ? : / To instruct Search to interpret any of these characters literally, rather as a special character, precede the character with a backslash character **\** For example, the term *web -based* will search for *web NOT base* so either remove the space before - or escape it **web \-based** to find web-based documents. Another example, *complexity n^2* is best to be searched with escaping **complexity n\^2** as ^ is interpreted as boost a term.

AIM Media House on Instagram: "Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has announced plans to build a government-backed AI university, an AI innovation hub, and a green data centre in the state. Speaking at Google I/O Connect 2026 in Bengaluru, he said Karnataka wants to become "one of the world's leading centres of responsible artificial intelligence."

Shivakumar noted Karnataka contributes nearly 40% of India's software exports and hosts over 17,000 startups. He invited Google to deepen its partnership, saying, "I am ready to give you any support you want," adding that Google employs over 18,000 people in India, with 12,000 in Bengaluru.

Google also rolled out AI initiatives for India, including on-premises Gemini access, Gemini 3.5 Flash, expanded language support, and new cybersecurity tools.

content: এআই পৃথিবীতে সেকেলে শিক্ষানীতি বদলে ফেলছে চিন। ২০২১ থেকে ২০২৫ সালের মধ্যে ১২, ২০০টি পুরনো স্নাতক ডিগ্রির পাঠক্রম বন্ধ করে দিয়েছে শি জিন পিংয়ের দেশ। শেষ পরন্ত যুগের দাবি মেনে ভারতও কতকটা সেই পথে হাঁটল। পথ দেখাল দক্ষিণের রাজ্য কর্নাটক। শুক্রবার মুখ্যমন্ত্রী ডিকে শিবকুমার জানালেন, বেঙ্গালুরুতে তৈরি হবে দেশের প্রথম এআই বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়। এই কাজে সহযোগী করা হবে বেসরকারি প্রযুক্তি সংস্থাগুলিকে। এর জন্য বেঙ্গালুরু-সহ গোটা কর্নাটকের পরিকাঠামো বদলে ফেলা হবে। শুক্রবার বিভিন্ন সংস্থার কর্তাদের সঙ্গে বৈঠকে করেন কর্নাটকের মুখ্যমন্ত্রী। সেখানে শিবকুমার বলেন, বেঙ্গালুরুর সবচেয়ে বড় শক্তি হল দক্ষ জনশক্তি ও উদ্ভাবনী পরিবেশ। ভারতের প্রযুক্তি-রাজধানী হিসেবে শহরটির উত্থানের কৃতিত্ব স্থানীয় মানুষ ও সংস্থাগুলির। শিবকুমার বলেন, আপনারেই বেঙ্গালুরু এবং কর্নাটকের দূত। কয়েক দশক আগে যারা এই শহরে এসেছিলেন, তাঁরা এখানকার সুযোগ-সুবিধা ও প্রতিভার উপস্থিতির কারণেই এখানে থেকে গিয়েছেন। ### আরও পড়ুন: মুখ্যমন্ত্রী শিবকুমার বলেন, সরকার ইতিমধ্যেই ডিপ-টেক, ডিজিটাল পরিকাঠামো, গবেষণা, শিল্প ও শিক্ষাপ্রতিষ্ঠানের মধ্যে সহযোগিতায় নতুন আইটি, মহাকাশ প্রযুক্তি ও স্টার্টআপ নীতি চালু করেছে। পাশাপাশি উদীয়মান প্রযুক্তির বাণিজ্যিকীকরণের গতি বাড়াতে কর্ণাটক তাদের ‘কোয়ান্টাম রোডম্যাপ’ও প্রকাশ করেছে। শিবকুমার আরও জানান, শিল্পক্ষেত্রের সঙ্গে অংশীদারিত্বের ভিত্তিতে রাজ্য একটি এআই বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় গড়ে তুলছে। শিবকুমার ‘বেঙ্গালুরু রোবোটিক্স অ্যান্ড ইনোভেশন জোন’ এবং ‘টেকসই ডেটা সেন্টার নীতি ২০২৬-৩১’-এর কথাও ঘোষণা করেন। এই উদ্যোগগুলোর লক্ষ্য হল জমি, বিদ্যুৎ, জল,যোগাযোগ ব্যবস্থা এবং পুনর্নবীকরণ শক্তির সহায়তায় পরিবেশগতভাবে টেকসই ডিজিটাল পরিকাঠামো গড়ে তোলা। আঞ্চলিক উন্নয়নের ভারসাম্যের ওপর গুরুত্বারোপ করে কর্নাটকের মুখ্যমন্ত্রী বলেন যে, উন্নয়নের ধারা কেবল বেঙ্গালুরুর মধ্যেই সীমাবদ্ধ থাকা উচিত নয়। কর্নাটকজুড়ে তা ছড়িয়ে দেওয়া হবে। ### সর্বশেষ খবর * #### ব্যর্থতা কাটিয়ে পরপর জয়, টি-টোয়েন্টিতে শীর্ষস্থান ফিরে পেল টিম ইন্ডিয়া * #### পদ নয়, বিজেপির কাছে শিক্ষার্থীরাই গুরুত্বপূর্ণ, ধর্মেন্দ্রর ইস্তফার পর বড় বার্তা শাহের * #### তৃণমূল সরকার অর্থ বরাদ্দ না করায় ফাঁকা নার্সারি! সবুজায়নে চারা কিনতে দিশাহারা বন দপ্তর * #### প্রতিদিন গঙ্গায় মৃত্যু চারজনের! ৬০ ফুট জলের তলায় ডিউটির অভিজ্ঞতা শোনালেন ডুবুরিরা * #### এইচওয়ানবি ভিসা ফি বৃদ্ধির প্রস্তাব খারিজ! মার্কিন আদালতে ধাক্কা ট্রাম্পের

title: Karnataka Announces India's First Public AI University in Bengaluru | L K Atheeq posted on the topic | LinkedIn
content: Today Karnataka CM Shri D K Shivakumar announced the setting up of the Bengaluru University of Artificial Intelligence (BUAI) on a 100 acre campus together with a AI Hub. It is ambitiously billed as India’s first and the largest public University of AI. The University should be a modern institution with new age governance structures which are flat, inclusive, collaborative and multi-disciplinary. The University can have 5 pillars: 1. Build AI, 2. Provide AI education at under-graduate, post graduate and skill development levels 3. Research on Use AI for key use-cases such as AI in education, healthcare, agriculture, climate and weather, manufacturing, Banking and other services etc. 4. Commercialisation of AI applications to real business problems through incubation, strong industry, academia collaboration 5. AI & Human Society: Ethical, political, social and political implications of AI and its applications to day to day life. The University can be a large workshop for education, research and skills and can have active private sector participation though the University will be public sector led. The AI Hub should be co-located and we should democratise access to AI through public libarary for AI knowledge, GPU credits, and affordable sand-boxes for start ups to try their ideas. These are ideas and concepts I am putting out in public domain to ignite a debate and to seek ideas. These of course are not Government views yet. #AI #Karnataka #Bengaluru #Education A good initiative. As this need to be be part of daily activities, we should look at integrating into the existing SSA/DPI, first grade colleges and to the engineering colleges through department of Collegiate and technical education Super...All the other states should follow. Very nice initiative sir and need of the hour when foreign universities have already come to Bangalore and functioning full fledged. Just that this university statutes must be different from “typical” public universities and must be real outcome based.

AIM Media House on Instagram: "D.K. Shivakumar says Karnataka will build India's first government-led AI University and a next-generation green data centre as Google I/O Connect India 2026 kicks off in Bengaluru.

Speaking at the event, the Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister said the state is laying the foundation for AI learning from the school level. He announced plans for the AI University, an AI innovation hub, and said AI education will be introduced in primary schools to help build the next generation of AI talent.

Shivakumar also highlighted Karnataka's human capital as its biggest strength and said a next-generation green data centre is being planned near Bengaluru. Praising Google's impact, he said, "Some companies build products, Google has built habits."

content: Published By: Kishore GhoshPosted: 07:12 PM Jul 24, 2026Updated: 07:13 PM Jul 24, 2026 এআই পৃথিবীতে সেকেলে শিক্ষানীতি বদলে ফেলছে চিন। ২০২১ থেকে ২০২৫ সালের মধ্যে ১২, ২০০টি পুরনো স্নাতক ডিগ্রির পাঠক্রম বন্ধ করে দিয়েছে শি জিন পিংয়ের দেশ। শেষ পরন্ত যুগের দাবি মেনে ভারতও কতকটা সেই পথে হাঁটল। পথ দেখাল দক্ষিণের রাজ্য কর্নাটক। শুক্রবার মুখ্যমন্ত্রী ডিকে শিবকুমার জানালেন, বেঙ্গালুরুতে তৈরি হবে দেশের প্রথম এআই বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়। এই কাজে সহযোগী করা হবে বেসরকারি প্রযুক্তি সংস্থাগুলিকে। এর জন্য বেঙ্গালুরু-সহ গোটা কর্নাটকের পরিকাঠামো বদলে ফেলা হবে। Advertisement শুক্রবার বিভিন্ন সংস্থার কর্তাদের সঙ্গে বৈঠকে করেন কর্নাটকের মুখ্যমন্ত্রী। সেখানে শিবকুমার বলেন, বেঙ্গালুরুর সবচেয়ে বড় শক্তি হল দক্ষ জনশক্তি ও উদ্ভাবনী পরিবেশ। ভারতের প্রযুক্তি-রাজধানী হিসেবে শহরটির উত্থানের কৃতিত্ব স্থানীয় মানুষ ও সংস্থাগুলির। শিবকুমার বলেন, আপনারেই বেঙ্গালুরু এবং কর্নাটকের দূত। কয়েক দশক আগে যারা এই শহরে এসেছিলেন, তাঁরা এখানকার সুযোগ-সুবিধা ও প্রতিভার উপস্থিতির কারণেই এখানে থেকে গিয়েছেন। মুখ্যমন্ত্রী শিবকুমার বলেন, সরকার ইতিমধ্যেই ডিপ-টেক, ডিজিটাল পরিকাঠামো, গবেষণা, শিল্প ও শিক্ষাপ্রতিষ্ঠানের মধ্যে সহযোগিতায় নতুন আইটি, মহাকাশ প্রযুক্তি ও স্টার্টআপ নীতি চালু করেছে। পাশাপাশি উদীয়মান প্রযুক্তির বাণিজ্যিকীকরণের গতি বাড়াতে কর্ণাটক তাদের ‘কোয়ান্টাম রোডম্যাপ’ও প্রকাশ করেছে। শিবকুমার আরও জানান, শিল্পক্ষেত্রের সঙ্গে অংশীদারিত্বের ভিত্তিতে রাজ্য একটি এআই বিশ্ববিদ্যালয় গড়ে তুলছে। শিবকুমার ‘বেঙ্গালুরু রোবোটিক্স অ্যান্ড ইনোভেশন জোন’ এবং ‘টেকসই ডেটা সেন্টার নীতি ২০২৬-৩১’-এর কথাও ঘোষণা করেন। এই উদ্যোগগুলোর লক্ষ্য হল জমি, বিদ্যুৎ, জল,যোগাযোগ ব্যবস্থা এবং পুনর্নবীকরণ শক্তির সহায়তায় পরিবেশগতভাবে টেকসই ডিজিটাল পরিকাঠামো গড়ে তোলা। আঞ্চলিক উন্নয়নের ভারসাম্যের ওপর গুরুত্বারোপ করে কর্নাটকের মুখ্যমন্ত্রী বলেন যে, উন্নয়নের ধারা কেবল বেঙ্গালুরুর মধ্যেই সীমাবদ্ধ থাকা উচিত নয়। কর্নাটকজুড়ে তা ছড়িয়ে দেওয়া হবে। Subscribe Sangbad Pratidin News App খবরের টাটকা আপডেট পেতে ডাউনলোড করুন সংবাদ প্রতিদিন অ্যাপ নিয়মিত খবরে থাকতে ফলো করুন ## হাইলাইটস Highlights Heading Karnataka DK Shivkumar AI Advertisement

content: As Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-1 became the first Indian private rocket to reach orbit, Chief Executive Officer Pawan Kumar Chandana's old statement resurfaced where he laid out his vision for the company, describing it as the "Uber for space". In an appearance on NDTV Profit's The Disruptors show, Chandana was asked about an earlier comparison he had drawn between Skyroot and SpaceX, describing SpaceX as "the bus, or the train that carries satellites" and Skyroot as "the cab". He said the analogy captures exactly what the company is trying to build. So that's what we aim to be, you know, we want to become the Uber for space," Chandana said. "What we do is that satellite companies book the rocket, just like you book a cab, and then go to wherever they want." Typically if you want to go to your home, you don't book a train, you have to book a cab to go specifically to your place. So there are satellites who want to go specifically to certain locations in space. And we're Uber for them, where they book the rocket, put their satellite onto the rocket, launch to space and get them dropped wherever they want." Chandana argued that building a working rocket unlocks a far larger opportunity than satellite launches alone. "The only way to go to space today is a rocket," he said. "So the moment you build a rocket, you're open to all these markets — from launching satellites, to launching humans, to building factories in space, to building air data centers, everything." He said the core challenge Skyroot is trying to solve is cost and frequency. "The fundamental thing to be sorted out is build low-cost, regular rockets which can go to space on a regular basis, and we want to convert spaceflight as easy as air flight. #uberforspace #skyrootaerospace #pawankumarchandana #aerospace #indianaerospace

content: ## Swamy Annan's Travelogue's Post --- ### **Swamy Annan's Travelogue** July 14 at 8:51 AM Karnataka has unveiled an ambitious roadmap to position itself as India's AI Capital, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar announcing a series of landmark initiatives aimed at transforming the state's technology and education landscape. The biggest announcement is the establishment of India's first and largest AI University in Bengaluru. Spread across a 100-acre world-class campus, the university will also have regional campuses in Kalaburagi, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, Mangaluru, and Mysuru, ensuring AI education reaches students across Karnataka. To strengthen the state's innovation ecosystem, the government will also set up a dedicated AI Hub alongside the university and introduce a comprehensive Karnataka AI Policy. The initiative aims to attract global investments, nurture AI startups, and build a globally competitive artificial intelligence ecosystem. In a significant push towards future-ready education, AI will be introduced as part of the curriculum from Class VI onwards, giving students early exposure to artificial intelligence and equipping them with foundational skills for tomorrow's workforce. The Chief Minister also announced plans to establish two next-generation Green Data Centres, one in a coastal district and another near Bengaluru. These facilities are expected to enhance Karnataka's AI capabilities while supporting sustainable digital infrastructure. With investments spanning education, research, startups, and digital infrastructure, Karnataka is making a strong bid to remain at the forefront of India's technology revolution. #KarnatakaAI #ArtificialIntelligence #Bengaluru All reactions: 1 share Like Comment

title: Karnataka’s upcoming IT policy, expected to be finalised by July, marks a strategic pivot toward emerging technologies, with a ₹50 crore investment proposal for an Applied AI Centre over the next… | AIM
content: Karnataka’s upcoming IT policy, expected to be finalised by July, marks a strategic pivot toward emerging technologies, with a ₹50 crore investment proposal for an Applied AI Centre over the next five years. State IT Minister Priyank M Kharge told The Economic Times that the new policy will move beyond Bengaluru, focusing on decentralising growth and building digital infrastructure in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities. “The IT policy will focus on creating new economic accelerators beyond Bengaluru. Infrastructure is a problem with any growing city, and that was quite naturally raised by stakeholders,” Kharge noted. Cities like Mysuru, Mangaluru, Hubballi-Dharwad, and Kalaburagi are poised to benefit from this expansion. The policy includes a ₹300 crore fund-of-funds for startups and a ₹100 crore deep-tech fund. Supported by inputs from Ekroop Caur, the state IT secretary, and Nasscom, the draft envisions fostering innovation ecosystems across the state. Nasscom has also proposed a deep-tech fund structure with ticket sizes ranging from ₹50-₹200 crore to meet global standards. As the state gears up for the annual CEO meet, the draft policy is undergoing final reviews through the IT Vision Group. With a focus on AI, blockchain, IoT, and 5G, Karnataka is redefining its digital future with a forward-looking and inclusive IT strategy. Good initiative! title: Karnataka To Draft Data Centre Policy - BW Businessworld
content: ### BW Communities # Karnataka To Draft Data Centre Policy, Eyes AI University To Anchor GCC Push BW Online Bureau Jul 15, 2026 State finalises infrastructure framework for AI computing as GCC Summit 2026 charts next growth phase beyond Bengaluru Representative Image The Karnataka government is finalising a data centre policy aimed at building digital infrastructure for artificial intelligence and next-generation computing, a senior state official said Wednesday at the GCC Summit 2026 in Bengaluru. L.K. Ateeq, Financial Advisor to the Chief Minister and Chairman of the Bengaluru Business Corridor, announced the policy in his keynote address, alongside plans to set up India's first public sector-led AI University and an AI Hub for research, innovation and commercialisation. A Vision Group for the AI University, with significant private-sector participation, will be constituted shortly, Ateeq said. Ateeq also reaffirmed the government's plan to expand GCC growth beyond Bengaluru into emerging technology clusters across the state. Dr. Avinash Menon Rajendran, Managing Director of the Karnataka Innovation and Technology Society (KITS), said the state's next phase of GCC growth would rest on three pillars: the state's dedicated GCC Policy, the NIPUNA skilling initiative for emerging technologies, and KATALYST, Karnataka's facilitation mechanism for Global Capability Centres. 29 reactions · 9 comments | Karnataka has announced a major push to strengthen artificial intelligence (AI) education and innovation, with plans to introduce AI education from Class 6 and establish India's first government-led AI University in Bengaluru. Sharing the announcement on X, Chief Minister D K Shivakumar said the state is working towards building an "AI-native Karnataka" by investing in education, research and digital infrastructure. The proposed AI University will focus on developing skilled professionals in artificial intelligence and emerging technologies, while a dedicated AI Hub will support research, innovation and collaboration between educational institutions, startups and industry.

As part of its broader AI policy, the state government also plans to establish two hyperscale green data centres to provide digital infrastructure for AI research, cloud computing and large-scale data processing while focusing on sustainability. The government said introducing AI education from Class 6 aims to help students develop an early understanding of artificial intelligence and prepare them for future technology careers. While the vision has been outlined, details regarding the school AI curriculum, the university's admission process and the implementation timeline are yet to be announced.
